'''Thomas Michael O'Neil''' (born September 2, 1940) is an American [[physicist]] who specializes in [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11607028.html|title=O'Neil, T. M. (Thomas Michael), 1940-|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2020-03-07}}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
O’Neil obtained his bachelor's degree at [[California State University, Long Beach]] in 1962, and then his master's degree and Ph.D. at the [[University of California, San Diego]] (UCSD) in 1964 and 1965 respectively. From 1965 to 1967, he was a scientist at [[General Atomics]] and from 1967 at UCSD as an assistant professor and later a professor. From 1980 to 1984, he was on the advisory board of the Institute of Fusion Studies at the [[University of Texas at Austin]].<ref name=":0" />

== Honors and awards ==
O'Neil is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=O%27Neil&first_nm=Thomas&year=1996|title=1996 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|last=|first=|date=|website=American Physical Society|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-03-07}}</ref> In 1971, O'Neil was awarded the [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] by the [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sloan.org/past-fellows?L=..%252F..%252F..%252F..%252F..%252F..%252F..%252F..%252F..%252F..%252Fwindows%252Fwin.ini%25252500.jpg&page=494|title=Past Fellows|website=sloan.org|access-date=2020-03-07}}</ref> From 1979 to 1983, he was co-editor of the [[Physical Review Letters]]. In 1991, he received the [[John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research]] with [[John H. Malmberg|John Malmberg]] and Charles Driscoll for their studies of non-neutral plasmas.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/dawson.cfm|title=John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2020-03-07}}</ref> There is a video, filmed in 1987, where [[John H. Malmberg|John Malmberg]] and O'Neil describe their research.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Malmberg |first1=John H |last2=O'Neil |first2=Thomas M |title=Pure electron plasmas near thermal equilibrium (1987) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zqRmxi9GQWs |website=YouTube |access-date=7 May 2026}}</ref>

In 1996, he received the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] for "''seminal contributions to plasma theory, including extension of [[Landau damping]] to the nonlinear regime and demonstration of the importance of particle trapping; discovery of the plasma-wave echo; and pioneering studies of the confinement, transport, and thermal equilibria of [[non-neutral plasmas]], liquids and crystals. His theoretical work and active guidance of experiments with trapped, non-neutral plasmas provide much of the foundation for this branch of plasma physics''".<ref name=":1" />
